items.headline: 海史密斯晚年真實樣貌
items.context: 一部由海倫·米蘭（Helen Mirren）主演的新片，探討了犯罪小說家派翠西亞·海史密斯（Patricia Highsmith）晚年的生活，並問她是否真的像傳聞中那樣粗魯難相處。認識她的編輯與出版人，紛紛出面回憶往事。其中出版人奧托·潘澤勒（Otto Penzler）說，他一直很喜歡海史密斯的作品，但兩人第一次見面卻是一場空。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: A new film starring Helen Mirren explores the Ripley writer’s later years, but was she really so rude and eccentric? Editors and publishers who worked with her look back Publisher and bookseller Otto Penzler has loved Patricia Highsmith’s work all his life, but their first meeting was a washout. In 1984, she agreed to give a reading at The Mysterious Bookshop, his store on West 56th Street in New York. The American author of the Ripley novels, then 63, had lived in Europe for 20 years – in England, then France, then Switzerland – and seldom made public appearances, so he had high hopes. “But no one showed up. We had maybe four people,” Penzler says from his book-lined office under the shop. Now 84, with a tidy white beard and a warm, amused manner, he is just back from a crime fiction convention and still very much in the game. Highsmith, he recalls, had little time for her readers. “She was somewhat taciturn. People got their book signed and left within five minutes. I had a two-hour event scheduled, so what does one do? With some authors, I can say, ‘Let me buy you dinner.’ Well, not with Pat.” She stonewalled his small talk about France with an “I can’t stand the bloody frogs”. Continue reading...

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Bristol Beacon The UK artist combines feminist fury with accessible melodies and a dramatic flair that sees her alternately pogoing and seeking out the wind machines at the prow of the stage People are dancing to a song they don’t know, with flower garlands in their hair and their arms around their friends. This reaction to Fairy Dance, an unreleased track written about the community that has sprung up around her music, says a lot about the moment Paris Paloma finds herself in, and tonight’s show feels for all the world like a stepping stone to bigger things. Throughout, Paloma leans in to the built-in drama of songs from her second album, The Fatal Flaw, which pairs ornate folk arrangements with the sort of arena-sized alt-pop production favoured by Florence + the Machine. With a sculpture inspired by surrealist Ithell Colquhoun ’s Tree of Veins dominating the stage, she falls to her knees to deliver high notes and seeks out wind machines at the prow of the stage, her flowing crimson dress buffeted as if on a wintry moor. Continue reading...

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: New exhibition restores painter’s place as leading figure in French movement that revolutionised art As a painter, friend, and collaborator of Edgar Degas, who exhibited with impressionist artists including Claude Monet and Camille Pissarro, Mary Cassatt was at the heart of the 19th-century movement that emerged in France and revolutionised art. She was also a woman and foreign – “American, American through and through” is how she described herself. As a result, in the 100 years since her death, Cassatt has been frequently overlooked in the country where she produced her best work. Continue reading...

items.headline: 北市長選戰週末雙星拚場
items.context: 九合一選舉進入最後兩週衝刺，台北市長候選人上週末在雨中大拚場。國民黨候選人蔣萬安舉辦「安心大遊行」，藍營重要人士齊聚力挺，主辦單位稱超過8萬人參加。民進黨候選人沈伯洋則在二二八公園舉辦「洋流祭」，邀請獨立樂團開唱，主打年輕選票。
